chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, he said:
When the boy reaches six years, salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him; then when he is able to fast, sawm (fasting) becomes obligatory upon him.

key_terms.أَطَاقَ: became capable or able to bear
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: the young boy or child being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the act of worship said here to become obligatory
key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: sawm (fasting), the act whose obligation is tied to ability
key_terms.سِتُّ سِنِينَ: six years of age, given as the threshold mentioned for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: At what age is a child commanded to perform salat (prayer) and when does sawm (fasting) become obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith states an age marker for a child’s salat (prayer) and ties the obligation of sawm (fasting) to the child’s ability to bear it. It addresses the religious training and obligation of children in acts of worship.
